properties.name: Kowno / Kaunas (Lithuania)
properties.description: Crossing the Niemen (Kaunas): The massive multi-nation Grande Armée crosses the Niemen River at Kaunas (Kowno, in modern Lithuania), marking the official start of the invasion. The Russian forces under Barclay de Tolly immediately initiate a strategic retreat, enacting a scorched-earth policy.

properties.name: Wilna / Vilna (Lithuania)
properties.description: Occupation of Vilnius (Vilna): Napoleon enters Vilnius unopposed. Extreme weather (searing summer heat alternating with violent, muddy rainstorms) immediately decimates horses and fosters typhus, crippling the French supply lines right out of the gate.

properties.name: Witebsk / Vitebsk (Belarus)
properties.description: Arrival at Vitebsk: Napoleon reaches Vitebsk. Frustrated by the lack of a decisive battlefield victory, he briefly considers halting the campaign until the following spring but ultimately decides to press deeper into Russia.

properties.name: Gross-Ekau / Lecava (Latvia)
properties.description: General McDonald On the northern flank, French-allied Prussian forces defeat a Russian detachment, clearing the path toward Riga.

properties.name: Smolensk / Smolensk (Russia)
properties.description: Battle of Smolensk: The first major collision of the war. The French successfully capture the holy city of Smolensk, but the Russian forces burn the vast supply stores and slip away unscathed, evading Napoleon's attempts to encircle them.

properties.name: Wizma / Viazma (Russia)
properties.description: The French continue pursuing the Russians through this town, which is torched during the retreat.

properties.name: Mojaisk / Mozhaisk (Russia)
properties.description: Located just past the Borodino battlefield, the French take this town and utilize it as a massive, overflowing field hospital for the thousands wounded at Borodino.

properties.name: Moscou / Moscow (Russia)
properties.description: Entry into Moscow: Napoleon rides victoriously into Moscow, only to discover the metropolis 98% abandoned. That night, fires intentionally lit by the city’s governor engulf Moscow, turning Napoleon’s ultimate prize into a hollow, smoky ruin devoid of food or shelter.

properties.name: Gloubokoe / Hlybokaye (Belarus)
properties.description: Napoleon sets up a temporary headquarters here for a few days to reorganize his rapidly tiring logistics chain.

properties.name: Polotsk / Polatsk (Belarus)
properties.description: While Napoleon is stuck in Moscow deciding whether to retreat, a major battle erupts far to his north. Russian forces successfully defeat Marshal Saint-Cyr's forces in the Second Battle of Polotsk, threatening Napoleon's primary line of retreat back to Europe.

properties.name: Dorogobouge / Dorogobuzh (Russia)
properties.description: The retreating Russians briefly consider making a stand here but decide the terrain is too weak and abandon it to the French.

properties.name: Chjat / Gagarin (Russia)
properties.description: Napoleon halts his army here for a couple of days to let his scattered columns rest and concentrate before the final push.

properties.name: Borodino / Borodino (Russia)
properties.description: The Battle of Borodino: The bloodiest single day of the Napoleonic Wars. Fought just 70 miles west of Moscow, the battle yields roughly 70,000 total casualties. The French secure a tactical victory, but the newly appointed Russian Field Marshal Mikhail Kutuzov preserves his army by executing an orderly withdrawal.
